domain: severe weather forecasting / NWS warning verification
prediction_question: For an NWS tornado warning at the moment it is issued, will it be verified - will at least one tornado report fall inside its storm-based polygon during its valid time?
prediction_time: The warning's issue timestamp. Everything the warning product itself carries at issuance is a feature: issuing WFO, forecaster of record, issue/expiry times (hence time-of-day and day-of-season), the warned county list, the storm-based polygon geometry (area, perimeter, polygon-vs-county size reduction), the tornado-possible flag on parent SVR warnings, the hail/wind tags, and - via the per-warning product-text URL - the full issued text (tornado tag, damage-threat tag, storm motion). The label is determined afterwards by which tornado reports occur in the polygon while the warning is live; the cow fields that encode it (verify, stormreports, stormreports_all, lead0, areaverify, statuses, status) are label-source/post-hoc and never ship as features.
target_definition: Binary: the per-warning `verify` boolean returned by IEM cow for phenomena=TO, significance=W - whether >=1 tornado local storm report (buffered by cow's default 15 km) falls inside the polygon during the valid window. The method is documented on the cow page ('NWS Storm Based Warning Verification') and matches the official storm-based verification concept in NWS Instruction 10-1601 ('FAR is the number of false alarms (unverified warnings) divided by the total number of warnings'; storm report points verify warning areas).

The verification label is IEM's computation over official NWS warnings and reports, not an NWS official verification product; any release must be labelled derived and must attribute IEM.
split_strategy: Temporal by issue year, all three windows contiguous and disjoint. Proposed: train 2008-2018 (storm-based polygons began Oct 2007), eval 2019-2021, holdout 2022-2024. Anchor measurements support capacity but window totals are computed at construction: measured 2013 = 1,832 warnings / 441 verified (24.1%) spread over 100 distinct days with >=1 verified warning; measured 2023 = 2,531 / 656 (25.9%) over 115 distinct days. Positives cluster by outbreak day, so the clustered count (100-115 independent positive days per measured year) is the figure that matters for window capacity, not the row count. Base-rate drift is a documented property of the source (warning POD peaked 2011, declined 2012-14, then recovered - WAF-D-23-0153), so multi-year windows and a drift note are required, not a single-year holdout.

preflight_2026_11_05.arkansas_fixture_correction_before_launc: The record's original fixture expectation ('the 2022-04-16 storm's warnings must read verify=false') was WRONG and is corrected BEFORE launch on measured evidence: (1) the paper at arXiv 2510.25011 is Wolff, Goodnight, Blind-Doskocil, Conklin, Gustafson, Trujillo-Falcon 2025, 'Reflecting on a Decade of Formalized Tornado Emergencies' - the record's 'Keylon 2025' attribution was a citation slip (Keylon 2025 is the performance.commerce.gov storm-based FAR KPI the same paper cites for the 0.69 all-warnings FAR). (2) The paper's own words: '3 tornado emergency false alarms, all of which were issued for the same nontornadic thunderstorm in northern Arkansas on 16 April 2022', 'false real-time reports of tornado damage' (Navarro 2022). (3) The IEM tornado-emergency archive the paper used (api/1/nws/emergencies.json) identifies the three 2022-04-16 UTC storm warnings: LZK #49 (00:09Z), LZK #50 (00:45Z), MEG #40 (01:05Z, states=AR) - one storm crossing the LZK/MEG boundary. (4) MEASURED cow verdicts on 2026-11-05: LZK #49 verify=TRUE, LZK #50 verify=TRUE, MEG #40 verify=FALSE - the false real-time tornado LSrs that later surveys reclassified as straight-line wind remain in the LSR archive and verify two of the three. CONSEQUENCE: the task label is REPORT-based (LSR archive), the paper's 0.03 emergency FAR is SURVEY-based (NCEI tracks); the 89-emergency 0.03-FAR cross-check is NOT expected to reproduce under the LSR label and is reframed as the documented semantics caveat. The pinned per-warning fixture asserts the MEASURED cow verdicts (1/1/0) plus the Joplin known-positive event.

measurements.nws_tornado_build_001_failure_diagnosis: CONSTRUCTION defect (row-key grain), not infrastructure and not a source-corruption event. The two 'duplicates' behind the refusal are two DISTINCT tornado warnings sharing (year=2016, wfo=GLD, eventid=38): product 201605262355-KGLD-WFUS53-TORGLD (issued 2016-05-26 23:55Z, parea 656.58 km2, stormreports empty, verify=false) and product 201605270019-KGLD-WFUS53-TORGLD (issued 2016-05-27 00:19Z, parea 4878.67 km2, stormreports 124,125, verify=true), issued 24 minutes apart across the UTC day boundary. Measured 2026-11-05 by probe/followup_2016_GLD_38.py (cow api/1/cow.json, wfo=GLD year 2016, phenomena=TO significance=W; evidence in probe/out/followup_2016_GLD_38.json; run log .factory/nws-tornado-build-001/container.log). So cow's (year, wfo, eventid) is NOT a unique warning key: each warning's own verify is correct for its own polygon/window; the pre-registered disagreeing-verify refusal fired on a false positive (distinct warnings, not one corrupted warning). Consequence for the rebuild: (a) the row key must become unique per warning (product_id, or (year,wfo,eventid)+product_id) and row_id must disambiguate them; (b) the dup_kept_earliest branch (agreeing verify, differing bytes -> keep one) can silently DROP a distinct warning - the same measured event is the test case, both warnings must survive as rows; (c) keep the byte-identical-dup drop and the disagreeing-verify refusal for genuinely same-product duplicates; (d) per-year row deltas in the failed run exceeded dup_identical for several years (2008 -6 vs 3; 2009 -10 vs 5; 2011 -51 vs 41; 2012 -33 vs 6), consistent with kept-earliest merges and/or unparsable-window skips - the rebuild's ledger must attribute every dropped row per year before relaunch; the raw-feature anchors (2013 1832/441, 2023 2531/656) are key-independent and unchanged. Cheapest discriminating next check (done): the single-WFO year pull above; next cheapest before rebuild is a local re-key of the cached anchor years 2013/2023 asserting the new key is unique and counting eventid collisions per year.

novelty_check.ours: Per-warning, issuance-metadata-only prediction of whether an NWS tornado warning will verify (>=1 tornado report in its polygon during valid time), full 2008-2024 history, frozen temporal splits, shipped as a scored runner contract for coding-agent evals; label is the publisher-computed per-warning verify flag with documented methodology
novelty_check.rule: A dataset that already exists in ML-ready form is not published. Mirroring is a failure mode, not a contribution.
